prompts.display_text: Pin a European country other than the UK whose Church missionaries left when World War I began in 1914.
prompts.text_original: When World War I broke out in 1914, Church leaders released the missionaries serving in continental Europe but left those in Great Britain in place. Pin a European country whose Church Global Histories chronology records its missionaries leaving or being evacuated when the war began.
prompts.citation: Saints vol. 3 ch. 11; Global Histories chronologies
prompts.note: Great Britain does not count: its missionaries stayed. Norway does not either: its chronology records only that fewer were sent.
prompts.summary: At the start of World War I, the First Presidency told European leaders to release German and French missionaries, and mission president Hyrum M. Smith then pulled missionaries out of the rest of continental Europe. Missionaries in Great Britain stayed. Local Saints across the continent led branches and preached on their own until the war ended.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: All North American missionaries left Germany during World War I; local members were called to preach (GH Germany, 1914-1919).

answers.name: France
answers.fact: All missionaries left; the French Mission was absorbed, August 1914.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Full-time missionaries were evacuated from Belgium during the war (GH Belgium, 1914-18).

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 1914.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Mission president told to release all missionaries, August 30, 1914.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Missionaries not native to Denmark sent home, October 1914.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Missionaries serving in the Netherlands were reassigned to safer missions (GH Netherlands, 1914-19).

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Missionaries from the United States left Sweden in October 1914; local Saints took over the branches.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 10, 1914.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Missionary work discontinued in 1914.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Last missionary in Brasso (Brasov) left after the war began.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose Church chronology records a foreign missionary leading or overseeing its first Book of Mormon translation.
prompts.text_original: Several early Book of Mormon translations were led by missionaries from abroad who learned the language. Pin a country whose Church chronology records a foreign missionary or mission president leading or overseeing its first Book of Mormon translation.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Japan, Hawaii, Mexico, Germany, Hungary
prompts.summary: Many of the earliest translations were missionary projects. Alma O. Taylor spent five years on the Japanese Book of Mormon (1904-09), George Q. Cannon learned Hawaiian well enough to translate it with Jonathan Napela, Daniel W. Jones began the Spanish work in 1874, and John Taylor directed the German translation in Hamburg.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Alma O. Taylor oversaw the first Japanese translation, 1904-1909.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: George Q. Cannon translated into Hawaiian with Jonathan Napela, finishing in 1854.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Under John Taylor's direction, George P. Dykes and George Viett began the German translation in 1851.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Brigham Young asked Daniel W. Jones and Henry Brizzee to translate portions into Spanish in 1874-75.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Arthur Gaeth, Czechoslovak Mission president, revived the Hungarian translation with a local member in 1931.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country with two or more missions of the Church (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: An African country with two or more missions of the Church at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025)
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 ten African countries had two or more missions. Nigeria led with 11, followed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (7), Ghana (6), South Africa and Ivory Coast (4 each), and Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Mozambique and Madagascar (2 each). Every other African country had one mission or none.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: 6 missions, 122,978 members.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: 11 missions, 274,043 members.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: 7 missions, 159,771 members.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: 4 missions.

answers.name: Ivory Coast
answers.fact: 4 missions.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: 2 missions, 24,547 members.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: 2 missions, 52,430 members.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: 2 missions, 39,282 members.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: 2 missions, 41,775 members.

answers.name: Madagascar
answers.fact: 2 missions, 20,395 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Spanish-speaking country whose first temple was dedicated in 2001 or later (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A Spanish-speaking country whose first temple was dedicated in 2001 or later (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Six Spanish-speaking countries received their first temple after 2000: Uruguay (2001), Paraguay (2002), Panama (2008), El Salvador (2011), Honduras (2013) and Nicaragua, whose Managua temple was dedicated in October 2026. Every other Spanish-speaking country with a temple had one by 2000.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: Tegucigalpa Honduras Temple dedicated 2013.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: San Salvador El Salvador Temple dedicated 2011.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Panama City Panama Temple dedicated 2008.

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: Asunción Paraguay Temple dedicated 2002.

answers.name: Uruguay
answers.fact: Montevideo Uruguay Temple dedicated 2001.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: Managua Nicaragua Temple dedicated October 2026.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where Church labor missionaries built chapels, schools or a temple in the 1950s or 1960s.
prompts.text_original: In the 1950s and 1960s the Church called young men as labor or building missionaries, trained in construction, to raise chapels, schools and even a temple abroad. Pin a country or territory where labor missionaries built Church buildings in that era.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: New Zealand, Australia, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Uruguay, Austria, Cook Islands, Peru; Samoa overview
prompts.summary: The building missionary program of the 1950s and 1960s sent young men trained in construction to raise Church buildings. In New Zealand they built the Hamilton temple and Church College; in Australia they built 19 chapels; others worked in Britain, Uruguay, Austria, Peru, Samoa and the Cook Islands.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Labor missionaries built much of the Hamilton temple and the Church College of New Zealand, dedicated in 1958.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: From 1956 labor missionaries were trained in construction and built 19 chapels across the country.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: In the 1960s labor missionaries and members built meetinghouses across Scotland, Northern Ireland and the rest of Great Britain.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Graz Branch members and labor missionaries built the Graz chapel from 1963 to 1965.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: On June 24, 1962, two members were called as building-construction missionaries under the building program begun in 1961.

answers.name: Uruguay
answers.fact: In 1961 the Church built the Carrasco block in Montevideo to house building missionaries.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: After World War II many Samoans served as labor missionaries, and Samoan labor missionaries built the first Cook Islands chapels.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Samoan labor missionaries built the first purpose-built meetinghouses at Avarua and Aitutaki, dedicated 1955 and 1958.
